member.name: M:Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry.ITelemetryClient.Flush
member.summary: Forces any buffered telemetry events to be sent to the ingestion endpoint. This is intended to be called once during shutdown rather than per-event: per-event flushing serializes the ingest loop on the network round-trip and can block subsequent events from being processed within the shutdown timeout.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Helpers.RuntimeFeatureHelper.IsMultiThreaded
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the current runtime supports multiple threads.
member.remarks:
Single-threaded WebAssembly runtimes (browser-wasm and wasi-wasm) do not have a thread pool: Task.Run continuations never execute while the single thread is busy, and blocking waits (Task.Wait / GetAwaiter().GetResult() on an incomplete task) throw . Code that would otherwise offload work to a background thread MUST fall back to inline/synchronous execution when this returns , otherwise the operation deadlocks or throws.
This is the single condition to branch on before calling ITask.RunLongRunning, creating a , or using a blocking primitive such as BlockingCollection<T>. Do not hand-roll an equivalent probe at the call site. There are two established fallbacks, and which one applies depends on whether the work is observable:
Best-effort background diagnostics (shutdown watchdog, slow-test reporters) are simply skipped. Scheduling them with Task.Run instead would not help: the loop would not run while the single thread is busy, and awaiting it during teardown would hang.
Work whose result is observable (the TRX streaming store's sidecar writer) is restructured to run inline on the calling thread. Note that swapping the producer/consumer hand-off for Task.Run is not sufficient on its own when the loop body blocks — the blocking wait has to be removed as well.
.NET 11 exposes System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.IsMultithreadingSupported for exactly this purpose (approved and implemented via ), and it is additionally a trimming feature switch, so it can light up dead-code elimination. The platform still targets earlier frameworks, so we derive the same information from the single-threaded-wasm probes, which are available since .NET 8. Once net11.0 is in SupportedNetFrameworks this property should forward to the BCL API under a #if NET11_0_OR_GREATER.
